examples.en: The interviewer's question made me nervous.
That news puts everyone on edge.
Don't make me nervous, I'm starting to shake.
The teacher tried to keep the students on their toes on purpose.
Movies that keep you tense are fun.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 소리가 아이를 긴장시킬 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sudden sound can make a child tense.

explain: '긴장하다'는 내가 떨리는 것이고 '긴장시키다'는 다른 사람이나 상황이 나를 떨리게 하는 거예요. 같은 뜻으로 '긴장하게 만들다'도 자주 말해요. 반대로 마음을 편하게 하는 건 '긴장을 풀다'예요.

phrases.en: The loud noise made me nervous.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 긴장시키다, often used in conversation.

phrases.en: Please don't make me too nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 부담을 주지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to put pressure on you.

phrases.en: I'm sorry for making you nervous by calling you suddenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 긴장하게 만든 일에 대해 사과할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to apologize for making someone nervous.

explain_en: 긴장하다 is when you yourself get nervous, while 긴장시키다 is when another person or situation makes you nervous. 긴장하게 만들다 is a common alternative. The opposite is 긴장을 풀다, to relax.

examples.en: On Parents' Day, I sent my parents a flower basket.

examples.ko: 꽃바구니는 꽃병이 없어도 바로 둘 수 있어요.
examples.en: A flower basket can be set down right away without a vase.

examples.ko: 선생님 책상 위에 꽃바구니가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: A flower basket was sitting on the teacher's desk.
I also put a congratulations card in the flower basket.
Until what time is flower basket delivery available?
Flower baskets are pretty too, but I like bouquets.

explain: 바구니에 꽃을 꽂아 만든 선물이에요. 손에 묶어 드는 '꽃다발'과는 모양이 달라요. 개업, 어버이날, 축하 자리에서 '꽃바구니를 주문하다, 보내다'라고 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I ordered a flower basket for my mother's birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃집이나 인터넷에서 미리 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering in advance from a flower shop or online.

phrases.en: I got a flower basket from a friend on my birthday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선물을 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving the gift.

phrases.en: I gave a flower basket to my friend who opened a shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 축하하는 마음으로 주는 선물을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a gift given to congratulate someone.
phrases.en_equiv: give a flower basket as a gift

explain_en: It is a gift made by arranging flowers in a basket. It differs from a '꽃다발', which is a hand-held bunch tied together. You often hear '꽃바구니를 주문하다, 보내다' for openings, Parents' Day and celebrations.

examples.en: Draw a diagonal line in the rectangle.
Don't cross the road diagonally.
The two diagonals meet in the middle.
Which diagonal is longer?
I folded the paper diagonally to make a triangle.

examples.ko: 대각선에 있는 가게가 우리 집 단골 식당이에요.
examples.en: The shop diagonally across is our regular restaurant.

explain: 수학에서는 사각형의 마주 보는 꼭짓점을 이은 선을 말해요. 일상에서는 '대각선 방향', '대각선 맞은편'처럼 비스듬한 방향이나 자리를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The bank is diagonally across the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 설명할 때 비스듬히 마주 보는 자리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in directions for a spot across and at an angle.

phrases.en: I drew a diagonal line inside the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학이나 그림 시간에 선을 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in math or drawing when making the line.

explain_en: In math it is the line joining opposite corners of a quadrilateral. In daily life it also marks a slanted direction or spot, as in '대각선 방향' and '대각선 맞은편'.

examples.en: I move the luggage to the warehouse.
A staff member moved the patient to the bed.
Please move the car somewhere else.
You can move the photo with the mouse.
We're moving the students to the classroom.
I moved the chairs and cleaned.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 다른 곳으로 옮기게 한다는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '옮기다'가 훨씬 자주 쓰이고, 이 말은 안내문이나 설명서처럼 딱딱한 글에서 보여요. 목적어가 필요해요.

phrases.en: Please move your car somewhere else.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정중하게 옮겨 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask someone to move something.

phrases.en: The teacher moved the students to the auditorium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 다른 곳으로 가게 할 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used when making people go to another place.

phrases.en: I move the desk to the window.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 이동시키다 and much more common in daily life.

explain_en: It means causing a person or object to move elsewhere. In daily life, the plain native verb for 'move' is far more common, and this one shows up in notices and manuals. It always takes an object.

dis.h: cause to move; formal, instructions or systems

examples.en: I looked at old sculptures at the museum.

examples.ko: 공원 한가운데에 큰 조각품이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A large sculpture stands in the middle of the park.
They say this sculpture was made from a single piece of wood.

examples.ko: 친구가 여행 기념으로 작은 조각품을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: My friend bought a small sculpture as a souvenir of the trip.
Is it okay to take photos in front of the sculpture?
Do you want to go to the sculpture exhibition together?

explain: '조각'이 만드는 일이나 예술 분야를 말한다면 '조각품'은 완성된 작품이에요. 사람이나 동물 모양이면 '조각상'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: A big statue stands in the square.
phrases.nuance_en: A sculpture shaped like a person or an animal.

phrases.en: My father makes sculptures out of wood.
The art museum is displaying new sculptures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품을 사람들에게 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing works to the public.

explain_en: While '조각' can refer to the act or the art field of carving, '조각품' is the finished work. If it takes the shape of a person or animal, it is also called '조각상'.
